{"path":"README.md","artifact":"1bc3059364e544bf248b8e1fee783225","numberedSource":"1: # Blindsight: an evidence-driven anatomy engine
2: 
3: Edit the root **TARGET.json**. Set `target` to a local directory/file, a public
4: GitHub repository URL, or one public HTTPS document. Keep `ref` separate from a
5: GitHub URL. Set `mode` to `replica` to also produce a source snapshot and mock.
6: 
7: The Blindsight reference is an engineering metaphor: many narrow reflexes leave
8: shared traces; those traces activate other workers. It is not a claim of
9: unconscious cognition, AGI, universal replication, or unprecedented research.
10: 
11: ## Start
12: 
13: From the repository root, with Node 22.13+:
14: 
15: ```bash
16: node substrate/bin/blindsight.mjs watch
17: ```
18: 
19: Leave it running. Saving valid TARGET.json starts a run within about half a
20: second when idle. Edits during a run are picked up after that run finishes; the
21: latest saved target wins. An empty target is idle. A malformed edit is ignored
22: until valid. The watcher needs a running computer or cloud process.
23: 
24: ```json
25: {"target":"https://github.com/Vector3on/ScoutIq","ref":"master","mode":"replica"}
26: ```
27: 
28: Local file paths are resolved relative to TARGET.json. Other configuration fields
29: can be omitted; defaults are bounded. Relative paths for cloud runs refer to the
30: Actions checkout, not your laptop.
31: 
32: ```bash
33: node substrate/bin/blindsight.mjs run
34: node substrate/bin/blindsight.mjs status
35: node substrate/bin/blindsight.mjs export
36: ```
37: 
38: The GitHub workflow automatically runs when TARGET.json is **committed** on
39: `codex/blindsight-autonomous-anatomy`, `master`, or `main`. A local save is not a
40: GitHub event. Runner queue time applies. Workflow dispatch is also declared;
41: the UI button generally requires the workflow on the default branch. There is
42: no promise of instant cloud compute and no polling cron wasting minutes.
43: 
44: The workflow validates the engine and persists the SQLite database and outputs
45: to the separate `blindsight-data` branch. It requires repository contents-write
46: permission for Actions. It serializes state writers, never force-pushes, and
47: never merges into the source branch. For public repositories those results are
48: public: use cloud runs for public material. Sensitive local material belongs in
49: a local checkout or private repository. Outputs have ordinary Git history, so
50: large repeated captures grow that branch. A workflow failure is visible rather
51: than silently reported as success; partial/budget runs exit 2 but still save.
52: 
53: ## What the workers actually do
54: 
55: | Layer | Mechanism | Limits |
56: |---|---|---|
57: | Surface | Bounded inventory, hashes, paths, captured bytes | Text only; excluded directories and binary files recorded |
58: | Structure | Directories, local import resolution, cycle detection | Import resolution is heuristic; aliases and dynamic imports can remain unresolved |
59: | Dependencies | package.json groups, import statements, manifest lines | Non-JSON manifests are lexical, not complete package resolution |
60: | Contracts | OpenAPI JSON methods/responses and route declarations | Code routes are candidates; not all frameworks or mount prefixes are supported |
61: | Data | Recursive JSON shape, SQL table declaration candidates | JSON capped at 1,500 nodes, depth 12, 100 children per node; no semantic schema guarantee |
62: | Implementation | Named declarations in common source languages | Lexical extraction, not a complete parser/typechecker |
63: | Operations | Scripts, environment variable names, container/CI declarations | Never executes scripts, installations, or target code |
64: | Seams | Boundary-related lexical evidence | Candidates, not verified trust boundaries or vulnerabilities |
65: | Semantics | Optional model interpretations with exact source quotes | Inferred only; valid citations do not prove a conclusion |
66: 
67: Each artifact fans out into suitable workers. Dependency observations activate
68: linking; the resulting graph activates cycle analysis. Attention weights
69: unresolved references and boundary candidates to select scarce model calls.
70: The SQLite queue deduplicates tasks, leases work atomically, and retains pending
71: work. Restarting after a task/time budget resumes the same source snapshot.
72: Interrupted leases expire after 60 seconds. Failed tasks remain visible; change
73: `refresh` to a new value to deliberately create a fresh run and retry them.
74: 
75: Stop reasons are explicit: `quiescent` (current worker frontier exhausted),
76: `budget` (work remains), `partial` (omissions/worker failures), `empty`, or `idle`.
77: Quiescence is a plateau of these extractors on captured material, not knowledge
78: of everything. Repeat runs still acquire source to detect edits, but unchanged
79: artifacts reuse completed extraction tasks. There is no claim of a distributed
80: swarm: this version schedules small workers in one process; SQLite leases are
81: ready for multiple claimants, but multiple CLI runs use a process lock.
82: 
83: ## Database and outputs
84: 
85: Default database: `substrate/.loam/blindsight.db`, compatible with Loam's
86: existing events table. The engine adds only `bs_*` tables/views. It does not
87: alter bounty scoring, migrate an existing remote database, or publish the site.
88: 
89: - `bs_runs`: status and coverage of each captured snapshot.
90: - `bs_artifacts`: sanitized source, metadata and content identity.
91: - `bs_facts`: entity, layer, predicate, typed JSON value, status, evidence, worker.
92: - `bs_tasks`: queue state, priority, attempts, lease and error.
93: - `bs_fields`: dynamically discovered field names and value types.
94: - `bs_entity_attributes`: observed attributes grouped into JSON arrays per entity.
95: 
96: New concepts become new typed attributes automatically. This avoids unsafe
97: dynamic SQL and column-count ceilings while preserving many values per field.
98: All queries use bound parameters for values.
